title: One cell, many doublings
prompts: Set rate to 1 and compare 5 steps (32 cells) with 6 (64 cells): the last step supplies half the final population.
At rate 1, read each step as 20 minutes; 6 steps represent two hours.
Set rate to 0.5: each step multiplies by the square root of 2, so doubling takes two steps.
Compare the blue reference 1 + rate × steps with the yellow 2^(rate × steps); their initial slopes are not equal.
Change capacity: in this doubling-mode lab it does not limit growth; the fixed mode parameter must be logistic to use capacity.
